title: Checks for identifiers which consist of a single character (or fewer than the configured threshold).
summary: To improve readability by requiring that every variable has a name more specific than a single letter can be. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for expressions where std::cmp::min and max are used to clamp values, but switched so that the result is constant.
summary: This is in all probability not the intended outcome. At the least it hurts readability of the code. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Nothing.
summary: This lint has been deprecated Clippy puts this lint in the deprecated group, at the level none.

title: Checks for usage of T::BITS - x.leading_zeros() where T and x are of different types.
summary: Substracting leading_zeros from the number of bits of another type might be a buggy implementation of the bit_width method. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for type parameters which are positioned inconsistently between a type definition and impl block.
summary: Specifically, a parameter in an impl block which has the same name as a parameter in the type def, but is in a different place. Type parameters are determined by their position rather than name. Naming type parameters inconsistently may cause you to refer to the wrong type parameter. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for getter methods that return a field that doesn’t correspond to the name of the method, when there is a field’s whose name matches that of the method.
summary: It is most likely that such a method is a bug caused by a typo or by copy-pasting. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for a op= a op b or a op= b op a patterns.
summary: Most likely these are bugs where one meant to write a op= b. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks assertions without a custom panic message.
summary: Without a good custom message, it’d be hard to understand what went wrong when the assertion fails. A good custom message should be more about why the failure of the assertion is problematic and not what is failed because the assertion already conveys that. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for repeated slice indexing without asserting beforehand that the length is greater than the largest index used to index into the slice.
summary: In the general case where the compiler does not have a lot of information about the length of a slice, indexing it repeatedly will generate a bounds check for every single index. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Suggests the use of const in functions and methods where possible.
summary: Not having the function const prevents callers of the function from being const as well. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Suggests to use const in thread_local! macro if possible.
summary: The thread_local! macro wraps static declarations and makes them thread-local. It supports using a const keyword that may be used for declarations that can be evaluated as a constant expression. This can enable a more efficient thread local implementation that can avoid lazy initialization. For types that do not need to be dropped, this can enable an even more efficient implementation that does not need to track any additional state. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Warns if there is missing documentation for any private documentable item.
summary: Doc is good. rustc has a MISSING_DOCS allowed-by-default lint for public members, but has no way to enforce documentation of private items. This lint fixes that. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for imports that do not rename the item as specified in the enforced-import-renames config option.
summary: Consistency is important; if a project has defined import renames, then they should be followed. More practically, some item names are too vague outside of their defining scope, in which case this can enforce a more meaningful naming. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks the doc comments of publicly visible functions that return a Result type and warns if there is no # Errors section.
summary: Documenting the type of errors that can be returned from a function can help callers write code to handle the errors appropriately. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for manual core::fmt::Debug implementations that do not use all fields.
summary: A common mistake is to forget to update manual Debug implementations when adding a new field to a struct or a new variant to an enum. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: It lints if an exported function, method, trait method with default impl, or trait method impl is not #[inline].
summary: When a function is not marked #[inline], it is not a “small” candidate for automatic inlining, and LTO is not in use, then it is not possible for the function to be inlined into the code of any crate other than the one in which it is defined. Depending on the role of the function and the relationship of the crates, this could significantly reduce performance. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks the doc comments of publicly visible functions that may panic and warns if there is no # Panics section.
summary: Documenting the scenarios in which panicking occurs can help callers who do not want to panic to avoid those situations. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for the doc comments of publicly visible unsafe functions and warns if there is no # Safety section.
summary: Unsafe functions should document their safety preconditions, so that users can be sure they are using them safely. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for empty spin loops
summary: The loop body should have something like thread::park() or at least std::hint::spin_loop() to avoid needlessly burning cycles and conserve energy. Perhaps even better use an actual lock, if possible. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Checks if a provided method is used implicitly by a trait implementation.
summary: To ensure that a certain implementation implements every method; for example, a wrapper type where every method should delegate to the corresponding method of the inner type’s implementation. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks if transmute calls have all generics specified.
summary: If not, one or more unexpected types could be used during transmute(), potentially leading to Undefined Behavior or other problems. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Warns for mistyped suffix in literals
summary: This is most probably a typo Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for items that have the same kind of attributes with mixed styles (inner/outer).
summary: Having both style of said attributes makes it more complicated to read code. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Warns on hexadecimal literals with mixed-case letter digits.
summary: It looks confusing. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for a read and a write to the same variable where whether the read occurs before or after the write depends on the evaluation order of sub-expressions.
summary: While [the evaluation order of sub-expressions] is fully specified in Rust, it still may be confusing to read an expression where the evaluation order affects its behavior. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.
